newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LAUDRUP OUTFOXES CELTIC IN 'OLD FIRM' DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAUDRUP OUTFOXES CELTIC IN 'OLD FIRM' DERBY.

text.p: A solitary goal by Dane Brian Laudrup saved Paul Gascoigne's blushes as Rangers beat Celtic 1-0 in an extraordinary 'Old Firm' derby on Thursday.
In a match notable for two penalty misses, numerous wasted chances and the sight of a wild fox running across the pitch, Rangers were hugely grateful to Laudrup's composure in front of goal.
His right-foot shot from outside the box after seven minutes gave Rangers the perfect start but it took some magnificent goalkeeping from Andy Goram to prevent Celtic securing at least a point.

Goram plunged to his right to save a penalty from Pierre van Hooydonk with five minutes to go, having seen his Celtic counterpart Stuart Kerr make a much more comfortable save from Gascoigne's tame spot-kick 17 minutes previously.

There was still time for an unaccountable miss by Dutchman Peter Van Vossen who blazed over an empty goal when unmarked eight yards out. Van Vossen was clean through again in injury-time, only for Kerr to smother the danger again.

"I don't think I've ever seen a game where we've had so many easy chances to score and missed so many," said Rangers manager Walter Smith, relieved by a victory which puts his team three points ahead of their bitter rivals at the top.
A passionate crowd of 50,000 also saw six bookings, five of them for Celtic whose manager Tommy Burns was banished to the stands after a touchline altercation with a linesman.

A two-minute delay as the stray fox tried to find an escape route provided another diversion, but ultimately it was the visitors' tactics of hitting on the break which proved decisive. Champions for the past eight years, Rangers have now extended their unbeaten run against Celtic to eight matches.
Van Hooydonk with 11 goals this season, will find it hard to believe he didn't salvage something from the spot with five minutes left.
Referee Dallas awarded the penalty when Richard Gough challenged Simon Donnelly but the cheers of the Celtic fans turned to tears as Goram pulled himself to his right to touch the ball away.
The goalkeeper has become a Rangers talisman in these fixtures, with Burns commenting last season: "They'll put that on my tombstone -- Goram broke his heart."
